## Type Aliases

### OysterCallerAccess

```ts
type OysterCallerAccess =
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "agent";
      policy: AppToolPolicy;
    }>
  | Readonly<{
      kind: "key";
      keyId: string;
      byInstallation: ReadonlyMap<string, AppToolPolicy>;
    }>
  | null;
```

The App-tool access one caller's catalog capture used, re-checked at call time
against a fresh read. An Agent's policy is one blanket level for every
installation (`host.appToolPolicy`); a key's is its own grants, resolved per
installation (`keyAppAccess`) -- an installation the key has no grant for is
captured as absent, never merely refused, so it is never listed at all.

### AppSurfaceCache

```ts
type AppSurfaceCache = (release) => Promise<ReleaseSurface | null>;
```

Per-host memo of each installed Release's catalog surface. A Release's artifacts
are immutable and content-addressed, so verifying the build, deriving its
operations and compiling its tool schemas happens once per Release ID and
artifact digest, not on every catalog capture: an MCP call captures the catalog
several times (refresh, session acquire, the pre-call authority check), and
redoing this for every installed App on each one exhausted a Durable Object's
CPU and memory. Only Release-derived facts are cached; installation authority,
caller access and tool-family listings are still read fresh on every capture. A
failed build is not cached.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                                  |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `release` | [`Installation`](apps.md#installation)\[`"release"`\] |

#### Returns

`Promise`\<[`ReleaseSurface`](#releasesurface) \| `null`\>

### oysterAppMethods()

```ts
function oysterAppMethods(
  host,
  principal,
  access,
  surfaces,
  preloadedInstallations?,
): Promise<
  Readonly<{
    id: string;
    acquire: (context) => Promise<
      Readonly<{
        snapshot: CapabilitySourceSnapshot;
        release: () => Promise<void>;
      }>
    >;
  }> &
    object
>;
```

Capture installed App methods for MCP or agents as one principal-scoped source.
Enabled installations become `env.<APP>` modules using the Instance call path; a
dotted method such as `repos.list` is `env.<APP>.repos.list()`. Visitors see
only public read methods; owners see every discoverable method. A key sees only
the installations its own grants admit, each at the level (`read`/`write`) those
grants give it; Mycelium itself refuses a write call up front when the module's
own grant is `read` (`mycelium/src/access.ts`). Call again to capture changes to
Releases, installation authority or the caller's own grants.

### oysterComputerTools()

```ts
function oysterComputerTools(host, principal): Promise<
  | Readonly<{
  id: string;
  acquire: (context) => Promise<Readonly<{
     snapshot: CapabilitySourceSnapshot;
     release: () => Promise<...>;
  }>>;
}> & object
| null>;
```

Capture the host's fixed Computer for one caller as a Knapsack source. The host
decides whether the caller holds Computer access; the Computer owner accepts
every call. Null when the host has no Computer or the caller has no access.
Grants name exactly the one captured module.

### oysterMcpCatalogLoad()

```ts
function oysterMcpCatalogLoad(host): (principal) => Promise<Readonly<{
  instructions: string;
  sources: readonly Readonly<{
     id: string;
     acquire: (context) => Promise<Readonly<{
        snapshot: ...;
        release: ...;
     }>>;
  }>[];
  grants: Grants;
}>>;
```

Load the current catalog for an authenticated owner or key: installed App
methods, plus the host's Computer when the caller holds Computer access. A key
sees exactly the installations and levels its own grants admit, and the Computer
only with its own `computer.use` grant; each App retains its own caller checks
regardless. The owner's stored write approval of an Agent's App tools is that
principal's confirmation for App writes, so a headless client can write; the
shared MCP server asks the client to approve every other write (an owner's own
calls, the Computer). Each call still re-admits the key, rechecks that same
stored approval, and passes the App's gate.

#### Parameters

| Parameter | Type                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`    | `Pick`\<[`OysterHost`](host.md#oysterhost), \| `"installations"` \| `"instances"` \| `"artifacts"` \| `"guestLimits"` \| `"backgroundOriginKey"` \| `"computerId"` \| `"computer"` \| `"capabilities"` \| `"appToolPolicy"` \| `"keys"` \| `"workflows"`\> |

#### Returns

(`principal`) => `Promise`\<`Readonly`\<\{ `instructions`: `string`; `sources`:
readonly `Readonly`\<\{ `id`: `string`; `acquire`: (`context`) =>
`Promise`\<`Readonly`\<\{ `snapshot`: ...; `release`: ...; \}\>\>; \}\>[];
`grants`: `Grants`; \}\>\>
